title: PraisonAI MultiEdit Writing to Persistence File
id: 4a7d9c3e-2b5f-48a1-9c6e-7d4e8b1a3f29
description: Detects PraisonAI Python agent (vulnerable multiedit tool, GHSA-29w3-p9w9-wc47) writing to authorized_keys, shell rc files, cron, or sudoers - the persistence vectors explicitly called out in the advisory's Impact section.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-29w3-p9w9-wc47
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/18
tags:
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.t1098.004
  - attack.t1546.004
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: file_event
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|contains: 'python'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'praisonai'
      - 'multiedit'
  selection_target:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '/.ssh/authorized_keys'
      - '/.bashrc'
      - '/.bash_profile'
      - '/.profile'
      - '/.zshrc'
      - '/etc/cron.d/'
      - '/etc/crontab'
      - '/var/spool/cron/'
      - '/etc/sudoers'

falsepositives:
  - Authorised IaC playbook that uses PraisonAI to provision SSH keys on freshly built hosts
level: critical

2500.datadog: source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:(SYSCALL OR PATH) @process.name:(python OR python3 OR pythonw) @process.command_line:(*praisonai* OR *multiedit*) @file.path:(*/.ssh/authorized_keys* OR */.bashrc OR */.bash_profile OR */.profile OR */.zshrc OR */etc/cron.d/* OR */etc/crontab OR */var/spool/cron/* OR */etc/sudoers*)

2554.sigma:
title: SocGholish Fake Browser Update Script Execution from Browser Download
id: 6c7d9b3a-2e41-4d2c-8f8a-1c2b3a4b5c6d
description: Detects wscript.exe/cscript.exe executing a JavaScript file from a user download directory with a browser as parent process - the FakeUpdates/SocGholish drive-by delivery shape.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/law-enforcement-nukes-socgholish-malware-from-nearly-15-000-sites/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0760/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/18
tags:
  - attack.t1204.002
  - attack.t1059.007
  - attack.initial_access
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\chrome.exe'
      - '\msedge.exe'
      - '\firefox.exe'
      - '\brave.exe'
      - '\opera.exe'
  selection_path:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '\Downloads\'
      - '\Temp\'
      - '\AppData\Local\Temp\'
  selection_js:
    CommandLine|contains: '.js'
  condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Corporate self-service scripts shipped as .js installers
  - Legitimate browser-distributed JS-based deployment tools
level: high
2554.spl: | tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe") AND Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe") AND (Processes.process LIKE "%Update.js%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%Chrome_Update%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%Firefox_Update%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%BrowserUpdate%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%.js%") AND (Processes.process LIKE "%\\Downloads\\%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%\\Temp\\%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%\\AppData\\Local\\Temp%") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

| ImageFileName=/\\(wscript|cscript)\.exe$/i

| regex("\\\\(Downloads|Temp|AppData\\\\Local\\\\Temp)\\\\", field=CommandLine) OR regex("(?i)(Update\\.js|Chrome_Update|Firefox_Update|BrowserUpdate|Edge_Update)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData], function=count())

2562.def:
// FortiGate SSL VPN logs typically arrive via 3rd-party MDE connector or surface in DeviceLogonEvents only when the VPN client logs onto the endpoint. Best-effort: surface RemoteInteractive/Network logons immediately preceded by VPN client connect, from non-corp IPs.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let KnownCorpSubnets = dynamic(["10.","172.16.","172.17.","172.18.","172.19.","172.20.","172.21.","172.22.","172.23.","172.24.","172.25.","172.26.","172.27.","172.28.","172.29.","172.30.","172.31.","192.168."]);
DeviceLogonEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ActionType == "LogonSuccess"
| where LogonType in ("RemoteInteractive","Network")
| where isnotempty(RemoteIP) and RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where not(RemoteIP startswith_cs KnownCorpSubnets[0])
| join kind=leftanti (
    DeviceLogonEvents
    | where Timestamp between (ago(60d) .. ago(LookbackDays))
    | where ActionType == "LogonSuccess"
    | summarize by AccountName, RemoteIP
) on AccountName, RemoteIP
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, AccountDomain, LogonType, RemoteIP, RemoteDeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

    | where DeviceAction =~ "login" or Message has "login successfully"

id: fcf7be01-8fdf-4f6f-efbd-7fb0dcfce6f9
description: schtasks.exe creating an ONLOGON task with /RL HIGHEST whose action invokes a script interpreter — Poisson's at-every-logon persistence pattern from the Cato CTRL writeup.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/junior-hacker-used-tailscale-and.html
author: thn-usecases
date: 2026/06/17
tags:
  - attack.t1053.005
  - attack.t1547
  - attack.t1078.003
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\schtasks.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'Create'
      - 'HIGHEST'
      - 'ONLOGON'
  payloads:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'powershell'
      - 'pwsh'
      - 'wscript'
      - 'cscript'
      - 'mshta'
      - 'rundll32'
      - 'regsvr32'
      - '.vbs'
      - '.ps1'
      - '.js'
  condition: selection and payloads
level: high
2623.spl: | tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name=schtasks.exe AND Processes.process="*/Create*" AND Processes.process="*/RL*HIGHEST*" AND Processes.process="*/SC*ONLOGON*" AND (Processes.process="*powershell*" OR Processes.process="*pwsh*" OR Processes.process="*wscript*" OR Processes.process="*cscript*" OR Processes.process="*mshta*" OR Processes.process="*rundll32*" OR Processes.process="*regsvr32*" OR Processes.process="*.vbs*" OR Processes.process="*.ps1*" OR Processes.process="*.js*") by host Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where user!="*$" | sort - firstTime
2623.datadog: source:(windows.security OR windows.sysmon) @Image:(*\schtasks.exe OR *\SCHTASKS.EXE OR *\Schtasks.exe) @CommandLine:(*Create* AND *HIGHEST* AND *ONLOGON* AND (*powershell* OR *PowerShell* OR *pwsh* OR *wscript* OR *cscript* OR *mshta* OR *rundll32* OR *regsvr32* OR *.vbs* OR *.ps1*))
2623.falcon: #event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\schtasks\.exe$/i CommandLine=/Create/i CommandLine=/HIGHEST/i CommandLine=/ONLOGON/i CommandLine=/(powershell|pwsh|wscript|cscript|mshta|rundll32|regsvr32|\.vbs|\.ps1|\.js)/i | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())

description: Creation/modification of an OpenSSH authorized_keys file on a Windows endpoint — the persistence step Poisson used to lock in key-based SSH reentry.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/junior-hacker-used-tailscale-and.html
author: thn-usecases
date: 2026/06/17
tags:
  - attack.t1098.004
  - attack.t1021.004
  - attack.t1078.003
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_name:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '\authorized_keys'
  selection_path:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\.ssh\'
      - '\ProgramData\ssh\'
  condition: selection_name or selection_path
level: high
2624.spl: | tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name="authorized_keys" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.ssh\\authorized_keys*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\ProgramData\\ssh\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Windows\\System32\\config\\systemprofile\\.ssh\\*") AND Filesystem.action IN ("created","modified","renamed") by host Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | sort - firstTime
2624.datadog: source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) @EventID:(11 OR 4663) @TargetFilename:(*\\authorized_keys OR *\\.ssh\\* OR *\\ProgramData\\ssh\\* OR *\\.SSH\\*)
2624.falcon: #event_simpleName=FileWritten (TargetFileName=/\\authorized_keys$/i OR TargetFileName=/\\\.ssh\\/i OR TargetFileName=/\\ProgramData\\ssh\\/i) | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())

2625.sigma:
title: certutil or PowerShell Certificate Store Enumeration
id: 1ef9da23-afa0-4f91-fbfd-9fd2fdfaf81b
description: certutil -store/-scinfo/-csplist or PowerShell Cert:\\ drive enumeration — recon for certificate-based / smart-card logins, the final-week move in the Cato CTRL writeup on 'Poisson'.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/junior-hacker-used-tailscale-and.html
author: thn-usecases
date: 2026/06/17
tags:
  - attack.t1555.004
  - attack.t1552.004
  - attack.t1087.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_certutil:
    Image|endswith: '\certutil.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '-store'
      - '-scinfo'
      - '-csplist'
      - '-csptest'
      - '-key'
  selection_ps:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'Cert:\CurrentUser\My'
      - 'Cert:\LocalMachine\My'
      - 'Get-ChildItem Cert:'
  filter:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '-urlcache'
      - '-decode'
      - '-encode'
      - '-hashfile'
      - '-verify'
  condition: (1 of selection_*) and not filter
level: medium
2625.spl: | tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name=certutil.exe AND (Processes.process="*-store*" OR Processes.process="*-scinfo*" OR Processes.process="*-csplist*" OR Processes.process="*-csptest*" OR Processes.process="*-key*" OR Processes.process="*-user*My*")) OR ((Processes.process_name=powershell.exe OR Processes.process_name=pwsh.exe) AND (Processes.process="*Get-ChildItem*Cert:*" OR Processes.process="*ls*Cert:\\CurrentUser\\My*" OR Processes.process="*Cert:\\CurrentUser\\My*")) by host Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where user!="*$" | where NOT match(process, "(?i)-urlcache|-decode|-encode|-hashfile|-verify") | sort - firstTime
2625.datadog: source:(windows.security OR windows.sysmon) ((@Image:(*\certutil.exe OR *\CertUtil.exe OR *\CERTUTIL.EXE) AND @CommandLine:(*-store* OR *-scinfo* OR *-SCInfo* OR *-csplist* OR *-csptest*) AND NOT @CommandLine:(*-urlcache* OR *-decode* OR *-encode* OR *-hashfile*)) OR (@Image:(*\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\pwsh.exe) AND @CommandLine:(*"Cert:\\CurrentUser\\My"* OR *"Cert:\\LocalMachine\\My"*)))
2625.falcon: #event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ((ImageFileName=/\\certutil\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/(-store|-scinfo|-csplist|-csptest|-key|-user\s+My)/i AND NOT CommandLine=/(-urlcache|-decode|-encode|-hashfile|-verify)/i) OR (ImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/Cert:\\\\(CurrentUser|LocalMachine)\\\\My/i)) | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine], function=count())

2677.sigma:
title: GCS Bucket Creation Matching Vertex AI Predictable Staging Name (Bucket Squatting)
id: 9a0c8e21-7b2d-4f31-9c4a-3b8e0f7a1d22
status: experimental
description: Detects creation of a Google Cloud Storage bucket whose name matches the pre-v1.148.0 Vertex AI Python SDK's predictable default staging-bucket pattern '<projectId>-vertex-staging-<region>'. Pre-positioned squatted buckets enable the Unit 42 'Pickle in the Middle' cross-tenant RCE attack.
references:
    - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/google-vertex-ai-sdk-flaw-let-attackers.html
    - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/hijacking-vertex-ai-model/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/17
tags:
    - attack.resource_development
    - attack.t1583.001
    - attack.t1583.006
logsource:
    product: gcp
    service: gcp.audit
detection:
    selection:
        protoPayload.methodName: 'storage.buckets.create'
    bucket_pattern:
        protoPayload.resourceName|re: '.+-vertex-staging-[a-z]+[a-z0-9-]*$'
    filter_uuid_post_patch:
        protoPayload.resourceName|re: '.+-vertex-staging-[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}'
    condition: selection and bucket_pattern and not filter_uuid_post_patch
falsepositives:
    - Internal teams manually creating staging buckets that follow Vertex AI naming convention
    - Migration / DR re-creation of legitimately-owned buckets in a new region
level: medium
2677.spl:
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Change where All_Changes.action=created AND (All_Changes.object_category="google_storage_bucket" OR All_Changes.change_type="Cloud Storage" OR All_Changes.object_attrs.method_name="storage.buckets.create") by All_Changes.object All_Changes.user All_Changes.src All_Changes.dest All_Changes.command All_Changes.result
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Changes)`
| rex field=object "(?<bucket_name>[^/]+)$"
| where match(bucket_name, "(?i).+-vertex-staging-.+") AND NOT match(bucket_name, "-vertex-staging-[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}")
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| table firstTime lastTime bucket_name user src result object

status: experimental
description: Detects pip / poetry / conda / uv installing google-cloud-aiplatform pinned to a version prior to 1.148.0 — the Vertex AI SDK release that closed the 'Pickle in the Middle' bucket-squatting vulnerability.
references:
    - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/google-vertex-ai-sdk-flaw-let-attackers.html
    - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/hijacking-vertex-ai-model/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/17
tags:
    - attack.initial_access
    - attack.t1195.001
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\pip.exe'
            - '\pip3.exe'
            - '\python.exe'
            - '\python3.exe'
            - '\poetry.exe'
            - '\conda.exe'
            - '\uv.exe'
    cmdline:

id: 7c4f8d12-9e3a-4b65-a2d8-1f0b3c8e9a47

description: Detects deployment of a Vertex AI model whose artifactUri references a Cloud Storage bucket outside the calling project — the persistence signature of the 'Pickle in the Middle' bucket-squatting attack.

            - 'google.cloud.aiplatform.v1beta1.EndpointService.DeployModel'

// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named
// in the article instead of a generic technique-class template.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName in~ ("node.js", "mscoree.dll", "msvcp140.dll"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,
          FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,

DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (FileName in~ ("node.js", "mscoree.dll", "msvcp140.dll"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath,
          FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

2683.sigma:
title: ClickFix Run-Dialog PowerShell Download Chain
id: 7f3e2a1b-9c4d-4e8a-b6f2-1d3c5e7a9b21
status: experimental
description: PowerShell launched from explorer.exe (Win+R Run-dialog paste) with a hidden window flag and an inline download cmdlet pulling a ZIP, Node.js, MSI, or .dat payload — the canonical ClickFix entry point used to drop BabaDeda, Lorem Ipsum, and Potemkin loaders.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/clickfix-campaigns-expand-malware.html
author: SOC Detection Team
date: 2026/06/17
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1566.002
  - attack.t1204.001
  - attack.t1059.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\explorer.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
  selection_window:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '-w hidden'
      - '-windowstyle hidden'
      - '-WindowStyle h'
      - '-nop'
      - '-noprofile'
  selection_download:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'DownloadFile'
      - 'Invoke-WebRequest'
      - 'iwr '
      - 'Invoke-RestMethod'
      - 'irm '
      - 'Invoke-Expression'
      - 'iex '
      - 'Start-BitsTransfer'
  selection_payload:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '.zip'
      - 'node'
      - '.msi'
      - '.dat'
      - 'mshta'
      - '.hta'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_window and selection_download and selection_payload
falsepositives:
  - IT admin Win+R PowerShell one-liners that download internal tooling

2704.def:
let SchtasksCreate = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName =~ "schtasks.exe"
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/create", "/Create", "-Create")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
    | project TaskTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName,
              TaskCmd = ProcessCommandLine, TaskParent = InitiatingProcessFileName,
              TaskParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
let DriverDrop = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where ActionType == "FileCreated"
    | where FileName matches regex @"(?i)^K[WX]1B5206BDC1743(FP|DD)\.dat$"
    | project DropTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DriverFile = FileName, DriverPath = FolderPath,
              DropProc = InitiatingProcessFileName, DropProcCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
SchtasksCreate
| join kind=inner DriverDrop on DeviceId
| where DropTime between (TaskTime .. TaskTime + 1h)
| extend DelayMinutes = datetime_diff('minute', DropTime, TaskTime)
| project TaskTime, DropTime, DelayMinutes, DeviceName, AccountName,
          TaskParent, TaskCmd, DropProc, DropProcCmd, DriverFile, DriverPath
| order by TaskTime desc
